title: Embedded inference MSA / DPA + cost pathing kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing path for embedded inference (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and pilot scope. Agreement to share redline + security pack and run a 2-week pilot with defined SLOs and test prompts.
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA + annotated DPA by 2026-01-12
Redwood to provide security whitepaper and SOC2 evidence link by 2026-01-10
Customer to share internal procurement timeline and PO thresholds by 2026-01-14
Schedule pilot kick-off (2 week) with Mina and Jess week of 2026-01-19
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir, Jess (Redwood); Chris, Dana, Mina, Omar (BlueMarble)

[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samir at Redwood, I'm joined by Jess, our solutions engineer. Quick check, audio and video okay?
[00:12] Chris (Procurement): Yeah, can hear you. Thanks for taking time.
[00:15] Dana (Legal): Good afternoon, audio fine. We'll keep this tight — legal and procurement priorities.
[00:20] Samir: Great. Objective for today: align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing pathing for embedded inference — specifically host vs dedicated pools vs private deployment — and sketch a pilot. If that matches, we'll dive in.
[00:32] Mina (ML): Sounds right. We want to run some latency and hallucination stress tests, and confirm data residency and key management.
[00:38] Jess (SE): Perfect. I'll call out technical constraints and what we need from your side for the pilot.

[01:05] Samir: Quick backgrounds — BlueMarble is evaluating Redwood for embedding our product recommendations and conversational assistant across EU and NA regions, correct?
[01:13] Chris: Yes — NA and EU, with eventual APAC but not in scope for this initial PO.
[01:18] Omar (Security): And we are strict on KMS integration and audit trails. We can't have plaintext keys stored by a third party, we also have egress fee concerns for large vector stores.
[01:28] Jess: Understood. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments and some dedicated options. For hosted we offer envelope encryption, and we can map out egress cost implications.

[02:00] Dana: On the MSA/DPA side — our counsel has a few non-negotiables: data processing scope, sub-processor list, incident notification windows, and punitive damages language around data exfiltration. We tend to push hard on 72-hour notice for incidents and absolute deletion assurances.
[02:22] Samir: We have a standard DPA that supports 72-hour notification, and retention/erasure clauses; Jess can follow up with the security pack which includes SOC2 report links and our sub-processor list.
[02:30] Jess: I'll include the whitepaper and SOC2 links. Note, some product names in our docs sometimes get scanned as Redwood Dedicate, but that's Redwood Dedicated — apologies if automated text munged that earlier.

[03:05] Mina: For pilot success criteria — we need 95th percentile generation latency under 180ms for our typical request size (avg 128 tokens), embedding throughput 200 reqs/sec with tail latency under 100ms, and semantic similarity recall at least matching our baseline (we'll provide the eval prompts).
[03:25] Jess: That's helpful. We can map those targets to a Dedicated pool with burst capacity or a Private VPC deployment depending on the latency variance you see. For 180ms 95p on hosted, it's tight but sometimes possible with optimized kernels and lower batch windows; dedicated gives more predictable SLOs.

[04:00] Omar: Important: if we go dedicated, we still need the data plane to sit in our VPC and keys in our KMS. What are the integration patterns and credential rotation mechanics?
[04:12] Jess: For Dedicated with VPC peering we deploy customer-dedicated serving nodes in the chosen region; keys can be customer KMS-backed, rotation is controller-driven and we emit key usage logs to your SIEM via our audit endpoint. For Private on-prem we provide an appliance bundle, but that has longer lead times.

[05:00] Chris: On pricing — procurement needs committed spend bands and rollback triggers. We can't sign an open-ended usage contract without a committed band and defined overage rates. What tiers do you offer?
[05:12] Samir: We offer usage-based for hosted, reserved capacity monthly/annual commits for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. Typical reserved bands give cost per token reductions and dedicated throughput guarantees. We'll send a pricing worksheet with commit tiers and an uplift chart for burst capacity.
[05:32] Dana: Also need to see SLAs mapped to credits, not just uptime percent. If there's degraded performance, what remedy exists?
[05:40] Jess: Our standard SLA maps availability to service credits. For performance SLOs — latency — we typically have playbooks to route to fallbacks and we can include canary-based rollouts. For enterprise deals we can expand SLAs with defined latency remediation and runbooks.

[06:22] Mina: We will almost certainly run evals that include adversarial prompts. How do you handle model fallback and audit trails for content?
[06:30] Jess: We support automatic fallback policies to smaller/quantized variants to maintain availability; all requests are logged (token-level tracing optional per config) and we can provide redaction hooks for PII. For hosted, logs are retained per the DPA; for private deployments you control retention.

[07:05] Dana: Regarding sub-processors — we need visibility into any cloud providers or CDN partners. Does Redwood use third-party inference providers?
[07:15] Samir: We run on customers' chosen hyperscalers in-region for hosted, and we own much of the runtime. We'll include the sub-processor list in the DPA appendix.

[08:00] Chris: Timeline — procurement target is to have legal sign-off by end of Jan, finance to cut initial PO mid-Feb. Is that realistic?
[08:08] Samir: Yes, if we get the redlines this week and circulate an annotated MSA/DPA quickly we can align. Send redlines by Friday and we'll respond within 3 business days.

[09:00] Jess — Technical deep dive start: For the pilot we'll need: sample request traces, a small labeled eval set, and an access window for one of your devs to run A/B calls. Mina, can you own that?
[09:12] Mina: Yep, I'll compile the evals and share keys for a staging dataset — no production data. We prefer v1 of the API and streaming disabled for consistent measurements.

[10:00] Omar: Security demo ask: can we get an architecture run-through showing KMS integration, key separation, and where audit logs emit?
[10:08] Jess: We'll do a short security demo during pilot kickoff; I'll prepare a diagram and sample audit logs showing key rotation events, request IDs, and retention policy.

[11:00] Dana: A couple redline items likely: limitations on liability, data destruction certs, 72 hour breach notice, SOC2 attestation and escrow for model weights? We might ask for escrow for critical models.
[11:18] Samir: Escrow requests are less common but we can discuss options. For model weights, many customers accept verification methods and signed attestations. We can escalate escrow logistics to the legal team.

[12:00] Chris: Egress costs — we need an estimate for vector store sync and batch exports. If we commit to a dedicated pool, are egress fees lower?
[12:08] Jess: Egress depends on region and underlying cloud. With Dedicated in your VPC you can avoid cross-region egress and often lower networking charges. We'll provide a sample egress calculator in the pricing sheet.

[13:00] Mina: One technical Q — do you support KV cache pinning or prefix caching for repeated contexts? That impacts token cost and latency.
[13:10] Jess: Yes, we have KV cache management and prefix caching; caching policies are configurable per model route and can dramatically reduce token costs for chat-like workloads. We'll include recommended cache configs for your use-case.

[14:30] (brief cross-talk: background noise)

[15:00] Dana: Contractually, our procurement requires a 30-day termination for convenience clause and normal transition assistance. Can Redwood commit to 60 days of transition support in the MSA?
[15:10] Samir: Standard is 30 days, but for enterprise we can extend to 60 days with a defined transition assistance addendum. We'll propose language.

[16:00] Jess: Quick note on metrics: We'll instrument latency percentiles at token and generation level, and push those into your observability via trace IDs. For the pilot we can share a dashboard template.

[17:00] Chris: Good. Next, procurement wants a single PO threshold for initial pilot <$50k, and any committed larger band needs exec approval.
[17:08] Samir: Understood. We'll price the pilot as a short reservedish token bucket, and show committed discount tiers.

[18:00] Mina: On model choices — we'd like the option to pin a particular open model version; can you guarantee rollback to previous model if quality drops?
[18:12] Jess: Yes, pinning versions and automatic rollback policies are supported. We also store model provenance and quantization profile so rollbacks are reproducible.

[19:30] Dana: Also need to confirm SSO/SAML integrations for account-level access and RBAC. We don't want shared tokens for dev and prod.
[19:40] Jess: We support SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC roles. We'll include the SSO integration doc and SCIM endpoints in the security pack.

[21:00] Samir: Quick recap — Redwood will: (1) send annotated MSA/DPA with sub-processor list, (2) provide SOC2 links and security whitepaper, (3) share pricing worksheet with commit tiers and egress calculator, (4) prepare pilot kickoff deck and security diagram. BlueMarble will: share redlines by 2026-01-09, provide eval prompts and staging data, and confirm PO thresholds and timeline.

[21:45] Chris: That matches procurement's view. We'll try to get redlines in by Friday but might be Monday depending on counsel.
[22:00] Dana: Legal will review, expect targeted redlines around liability and data destruction.

[22:30] Jess: I'll book a technical pilot kickoff for week of Jan 19 — propose Jan 20 at 14:00 UTC, will that work?
[22:40] Mina: Works for me.
[22:45] Omar: Works on my side pending calendars.

[23:00] Samir: Great. Any final questions or blockers?
[23:08] Chris: Not from procurement; just need the worksheet and DPA quickly.
[23:12] Dana: Make sure the SOC2 link includes sub-service organization controls if possible.
[23:20] Jess: Will do.

[23:40] (wrap)
[23:50] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials. Meeting adjourned.

Action items (formatted):
- Samir / Redwood: Send annotated MSA + DPA, sub-processor list, security whitepaper and SOC2 link (due 2026-01-10).
- Redwood (Jess): Pricing worksheet with commit tiers and egress calculator (due 2026-01-09).
- Mina (BlueMarble): Provide eval prompts, sample traces and staging dataset for pilot (due 2026-01-14).
- BlueMarble (Dana/Legal): Circulate MSA/DPA redlines (target 2026-01-09; might slip to 2026-01-12).
- Schedule pilot kickoff: Jan 20, 2026 14:00 UTC (tentative)

References / Links mentioned: "security whitepaper" (to be shared), "SOC2 report link" (to be shared), "pricing worksheet" (to be shared).

End of transcript.
